answer: A newcomer enters the economy only through a narrow inlet guarded by established peers: several existing agents must vouch for it, staking their own locked funds on its good behavior. If it cheats, the vouchers lose their stake, so trust becomes a scarce, priced resource rather than a free label. Forging a thousand fake identities means buying a thousand vouches, each costing real collateral, while honest vouchers earn fees for careful screening. No ivory-tower paperwork passes the gate — what matters is who stakes behind you, and like yarrow, trust only spreads where roots already hold.
